Pay attention to
• Deadline December 1 is earlier than many peers. No verified late-letter grace or time zone.
• US undergraduate study likely waives admission English testing but not TA speaking certification. Math and
central scales require reconciliation.
• Future 2027-28 stipend is unverified amid contract negotiations; historical fall/spring salary is not
twelve-month support.
• Faculty directory controls over stale prose group lists. Christopher Dodd's official current role is University
Laboratory High School visiting teaching associate, despite old algebraic-geometry listings.
• Bradlow, Kedem, Di Francesco, Berndt, Boca, Reznick, D'Angelo and Bergvelt are emeriti; independent new
doctoral advising cannot be assumed. Di Francesco's profile header still uses a distinguished-professor title,
but its Additional Campus Affiliations explicitly says emeritus.
• Iwan Duursma is emeritus; a recent individual paper was not verified because the personal page was
unavailable. His arithmetic-curves/coding background is retained as a historical contact, not a current adviser
assurance.
• Patrick Allen appears as an adjunct on older number-theory material; do not assume Illinois is his primary
appointment or that he admits Illinois PhD students without confirmation.
• Faculty leaves on an undated service list do not establish 2027-28 availability.
• Thorner's current institutional rank is associate professor; older personal biography wording is stale.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's completed before enrollment is an eligible direct PhD route; F1 status does not exclude
admission. Final-year applicants may be conditionally admitted. Central GPA minimum is 3.0/4.0 over the last
two undergraduate years; Mathematics typically does not admit below 3.25. Actual record and preparation
remain to be assessed. A master's is not required; an MS may be earned en route. [u1] [u7] [u8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD and Fall 2027. Prepare transcripts, three mathematics referees, academic statement
and central personal short answers; check whether the portal asks for a CV. No advance supervisor
sponsorship or research proposal is listed. Start references early; do not wait for letters to submit. Pay the fee
before the deadline unless an approved exemption applies. Resolve separate TA speaking certification even if
exempt from admission English testing. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior adviser consent is listed. Use current directory and individual publication pages, because several
prose group rosters are stale. Listed active faculty have unconfirmed Fall 2027 availability. Emeriti are
explicitly separated. Christopher Dodd is now a University Laboratory High School teaching associate; do not
assume he is a current Math PhD adviser from an old algebraic-geometry page. [u1] [u19] [u20] [u21] [u22] [u23]
[u30]

Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use choose.illinois.edu graduate application; enter institutions, upload records and statements, invite referees,
inspect rendered documents, then submit/pay. Do not wait for letters to submit. After submission, additional
documents may be uploaded through the status page, but notify Math and do not assume late materials will be
reviewed. Admission letters and final Graduate College notice appear electronically. Immigration financial
forms and bank evidence follow acceptance. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u4] [u18]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Math explicitly identifies Fall 2027 and December 1, 2026, with no Spring 2027 entry. Central handbook and
fellowship competitions are 2026-27; salary figures are 2025-26/2026-27, not 2027-28. Contract negotiation
update October 29, 2026 confirms future wage terms remain unsettled publicly. [u1] [u8] [u9] [u10] [u11]

sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [2027
confirmed]
December 1, 2026 for Fall 2027: application and all supporting materials, including letters. No public time/time
zone or separate grace period verified. Late or incomplete files generally will not be reviewed. No Spring 2027
entry. Ordinary support consideration accompanies the PhD application. [u1]

come from the testing agency and be within two years of the proposed program start. ETS institution 1836;

contact the department for receipt confirmation. Neither GRE is required. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u8]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Central admission table: new TOEFL 4 limited / 5 full status; old TOEFL 79 / 103; IELTS 6.5 / 7.5; DET 115 / 135.
Math additionally lists old TOEFL 95 total and 22 speaking, or IELTS 6.5 speaking, without a new-scale
conversion. Math encourages scores even from exempt applicants. TA certification is separate: new TOEFL
speaking 5, old 24, or IELTS speaking 8; institutional oral assessment is an alternative. DET does not establish
TA qualification. Math permits temporary nonclassroom TA duties for old speaking 22-23, with full teaching
qualification within two years; new-scale equivalent unverified. TOEFL Home Edition/IELTS Online accepted
centrally; Essentials, MyBest and IELTS One Skill Retake are not. [u1] [u3] [u8] [u15]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Admission exemption likely applies through at least two years of postsecondary US study within five years of
entry, or a US degree received within five years. Thus an on-campus UChicago undergraduate normally
qualifies; confirm actual dates and study location. This inference is not individual approval. The exemption
does not waive the independent TA speaking requirement. Math's encouragement to submit scores remains
despite central exemption. [u1] [u3] [u8]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Not required for Fall 2027. The department does not explicitly say scores are prohibited, ignored, or
recommended; do not equate 'not required' with 'not considered.' The central portal supports score reporting,
but Math's treatment of voluntarily submitted scores is not publicly resolved. [u1] [u2]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
List every postsecondary institution where credit was earned and upload each transcript/academic record,
including the latest completed term. If awarded degree is not on transcript, include diploma/degree certificate.
Non-English records require originals and English translations; preserve grading keys. PDF or Word uploads
must be legible; scan guidance recommends grayscale under 200 dpi and use View Document to inspect.
Uploaded credentials are unofficial. Official versions are required during the first term after admission, though
the university may request them earlier. [u2] [u8]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
No separate mathematics-course list or applicant-written course descriptions are listed on the current PhD
checklist. The department explicitly says no program-specific questions or writing samples are required. Supply
full academic records; verify any live-portal optional course field rather than inventing a separate requirement.
[u1] [u2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendation letters, preferably from mathematics professors who taught you or supervised your
research. Submit through the designated online recommendation system; Interfolio is not accepted. [u1] [u2]
[u4]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional reference is listed for ordinary TA consideration. Illinois Distinguished and Dean's Doctoral
Fellowships use departmental nominations, but the detail pages could not be fully read; additional nomination
references or questions remain unverified. Do not assume an extra applicant letter is required. [u1] [u6] [u11]
[u12] [u13]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Enter referees in the Recommendations section; letters can precede application submission. Public instructions
do not identify whether merely saving details immediately emails the invitation or a separate send action is
necessary. Check the live interface and ask referees before entering their details. [u2] [u4]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Applicant may submit before all references arrive; recommenders can upload afterward, but Math's December
1 deadline still applies. Invitations are not restricted to post-submission. Central FAQ supports adding or editing
recommender information and reminders. [u1] [u2] [u4]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Application status is available online, with reference management and reminder functions. A reference-specific
receipt badge or automatic applicant email for each letter is not described precisely in the public pages
reviewed; inspect the live checklist or contact the department if uncertain. [u4] [u18]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
A letter from another Illinois program or term may be reused only with the writer's explicit permission.
Importing the earlier recommendation does not send a new request, so do not import if a fresh letter is
intended. Referee email can be edited and reminders sent. An unsubmitted recommendation may be
excluded/reinstated; changing the access waiver requires excluding and re-adding the referee. Replacement of
an already submitted letter is not publicly established. [u2] [u4]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
Central instructions say most programs require a résumé/CV, but the Math PhD checklist does not clearly list it.
Prepare an academic CV and inspect the live required flag; no Math-specific public length or formatting limit
found. Do not import a separate internal-MS application's CV rules. [u1] [u2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required academic statement. Central guidance gives program-dependent maximums of 500-1,000 words; the
precise Math maximum is not publicly stated. Prompt paraphrase: preparation through
coursework/training/research; intellectual interests and questions; relevant faculty fit; how the program
supports academic/professional goals. Math calls its document a personal statement and asks for an honest,
brief, specific explanation of interest in Illinois. Treat that as the academic statement while also completing the
central personal short answers. Exact official wording is linked; no public font/spacing rule found. [u1] [u2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central personal short answers: each maximum 250 words. Questions 1 and 2 required, 3 and 4 optional.
Paraphrases: (1) pivotal experiences, opportunities or challenges, including access/financial barriers, shaping
education and professional development; (2) a concrete contribution or collaboration among people with
differing perspectives, abilities or experiences, its positive outcome and learning, in relation to
inclusion/belonging/respect; (3) explain if the record understates ability or clarify gaps; (4) add information
absent elsewhere or elaborate earlier responses. Verify exact current text in linked instructions and portal. [u2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Discuss interests and potential faculty within the academic statement. No separately required
research-interest essay identified. [u1] [u2]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
No mandatory research proposal listed for direct Mathematics PhD entry. [u1] [u2]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Department explicitly says no writing sample is required. A thesis, paper or research summary is therefore not
a mandatory item; optional upload/link treatment and limits are not publicly specified. [u1]
Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate mandatory publications list found. Include genuine research outputs and accurate publication
status in an optional/required CV if the portal requests it; do not assume full-paper uploads are necessary. [u1]
[u2]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
No separate mathematics-course list or applicant-written course descriptions are listed on the current PhD
checklist. The department explicitly says no program-specific questions or writing samples are required. Supply
full academic records; verify any live-portal optional course field rather than inventing a separate requirement.
[u1] [u2]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Ordinary TA consideration requires no separate scholarship essay found. Departmental nominations for Illinois
Distinguished and Dean's Doctoral Fellowships have award-specific materials, but publicly linked detail pages
returned JavaScript errors; exact supplementary prompts and limits remain unresolved. Ask Math before
preparing extra award essays. [u6] [u11] [u12] [u13]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Complete central personal short answers in addition to the academic statement. Illinois permits AI assistance
for organization, flow or grammar, but not substantive generation that replaces the applicant's own analysis
and voice. Public Math page says no extra program-specific questions; verify live portal. Prompt descriptions
here are paraphrases, not verbatim transcriptions. [u1] [u2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Math publishes a 2025-26 TA stipend of $24,620 for fall/spring, not a Fall 2027 promise. Central 2026-27
minimum at 50% is $24,200 for nine months ($2,688.89 monthly), or $32,266.68 over twelve months;
appointment duration matters. These carry forward rates effective August 16, 2025 while successor contract
negotiations continue. Illinois Distinguished Fellowship is indexed at $75,000 total; other official departments
describe $25,000 annually for three years, a standing cross-program description rather than a verified 2027
Math award. Tuition waiver is separate; ordinary summer income is not guaranteed. [u6] [u9] [u10] [u14] [u25]
[u26]
Years of support [Standing rule]
For entrants with a bachelor's, ordinary support may be renewed for six years, subject to satisfactory progress
and assigned duties. Entrants with a two-year master's generally receive five years. Summer funding is
separate unless expressly included in the offer. [u6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary assistantships and associated tuition waivers are available to international students, subject to work
authorization and TA English qualification. GAANN opportunities advertised for US applicants do not establish
F1 eligibility. Dean's Doctoral Fellowship eligibility was not fully accessible; do not assume F1 eligibility.
Financial certification for immigration follows an accepted offer, not the academic application. [u1] [u3] [u6] [u13]
[u17]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
A typical 50% TA entails about 20 hours/week: first-year assignments may include two two-hour discussion
sections, coordination, tutoring and grading. Full tuition waiver applies regardless of residency, with only
partial fee waiver; current health subsidy and remaining fees must be confirmed. Progress and
teaching-language qualification govern renewal. Department's approximately $1,700 immigration-budget gap
is an undated example; current I-20 costs and the actual award govern. [u1] [u6] [u15]
Extra funding application [2027 confirmed]
Ordinary support considered with admission. Department-nominated Illinois Distinguished and Dean's Doctoral
competitions: round 1 nomination deadline January 7, 2027, decisions February 12; round 2 February 18,
decisions March 30. These are departmental nomination dates, not substitutes for the December 1 Math
application deadline. Math's internal nomination cutoff and supplementary materials remain unverified; no
public time zone found. [u1] [u6] [u11]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Conditional summer teaching/research generally listed at $2,000-$6,000 for one to three months; adviser
grants, departmental awards, external/home-country fellowships and the campus assistantship clearinghouse
may help. Morisato Summer 2026 award offered $4,500 for six weeks to current Illinois Mathematics Lab team
leaders with at least two terms' involvement; this is not guaranteed entry funding. Older Equity Doctoral
Fellowship wording has been superseded by current Dean's Doctoral terminology. [u6] [u11] [u13] [u17] [u24]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$90 nonrefundable application fee, paid electronically before the application is processed/submitted. Budget
the current central fee and confirm portal amount. [u2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
International applicants ordinarily cannot receive an application-fee waiver except under an approved
exchange agreement. A US undergraduate degree alone does not make an F1 applicant domestic. Domestic
qualifying-program waivers are distinct. FreeApp requests for Spring/Summer/Fall 2027 are accepted only
before June 30, 2027 and must precede application submission; that later program date does not extend
Math's December 1 deadline and does not establish this applicant's eligibility. [u2]

fields.text: Conditional summer teaching/research generally listed at $2,000-$6,000 for one to three months; adviser grants, departmental awards, external/home-country fellowships and the campus assistantship clearinghouse may help. Morisato Summer 2026 award offered $4,500 for six weeks to current Illinois Mathematics Lab team leaders with at least two terms' involvement; this is not guaranteed entry funding. Older Equity Doctoral Fellowship wording has been superseded by current Dean's Doctoral terminology. [u6] [u11] [u13] [u17] [u24]

fields.label: Application fee
fields.text: $90 nonrefundable application fee, paid electronically before the application is processed/submitted. Budget the current central fee and confirm portal amount. [u2]

fields.label: Fee waiver
fields.text: International applicants ordinarily cannot receive an application-fee waiver except under an approved exchange agreement. A US undergraduate degree alone does not make an F1 applicant domestic. Domestic qualifying-program waivers are distinct. FreeApp requests for Spring/Summer/Fall 2027 are accepted only before June 30, 2027 and must precede application submission; that later program date does not extend Math's December 1 deadline and does not establish this applicant's eligibility. United States · Mathematics PhD

materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Deadline December 1 is earlier than many peers. No verified late-letter grace or time zone.
• US undergraduate study likely waives admission English testing but not TA speaking certification. Math and
central scales require reconciliation.
• Future 2027-28 stipend is unverified amid contract negotiations; historical fall/spring salary is not
twelve-month support.
• Faculty directory controls over stale prose group lists. Christopher Dodd's official current role is University
Laboratory High School visiting teaching associate, despite old algebraic-geometry listings.
• Bradlow, Kedem, Di Francesco, Berndt, Boca, Reznick, D'Angelo and Bergvelt are emeriti; independent new
doctoral advising cannot be assumed. Di Francesco's profile header still uses a distinguished-professor title,
but its Additional Campus Affiliations explicitly says emeritus.
• Iwan Duursma is emeritus; a recent individual paper was not verified because the personal page was
unavailable. His arithmetic-curves/coding background is retained as a historical contact, not a current adviser
assurance.
• Patrick Allen appears as an adjunct on older number-theory material; do not assume Illinois is his primary
appointment or that he admits Illinois PhD students without confirmation.
• Faculty leaves on an undated service list do not establish 2027-28 availability.
• Thorner's current institutional rank is associate professor; older personal biography wording is stale.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's completed before enrollment is an eligible direct PhD route; F1 status does not exclude
admission. Final-year applicants may be conditionally admitted. Central GPA minimum is 3.0/4.0 over the last
two undergraduate years; Mathematics typically does not admit below 3.25. Actual record and preparation
remain to be assessed. A master's is not required; an MS may be earned en route. [u1] [u7] [u8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD and Fall 2027. Prepare transcripts, three mathematics referees, academic statement
and central personal short answers; check whether the portal asks for a CV. No advance supervisor
sponsorship or research proposal is listed. Start references early; do not wait for letters to submit. Pay the fee
before the deadline unless an approved exemption applies. Resolve separate TA speaking certification even if
exempt from admission English testing. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior adviser consent is listed. Use current directory and individual publication pages, because several
prose group rosters are stale. Listed active faculty have unconfirmed Fall 2027 availability. Emeriti are
explicitly separated. Christopher Dodd is now a University Laboratory High School teaching associate; do not
assume he is a current Math PhD adviser from an old algebraic-geometry page. [u1] [u19] [u20] [u21] [u22] [u23]
[u30]

Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use choose.illinois.edu graduate application; enter institutions, upload records and statements, invite referees,
inspect rendered documents, then submit/pay. Do not wait for letters to submit. After submission, additional
documents may be uploaded through the status page, but notify Math and do not assume late materials will be
reviewed. Admission letters and final Graduate College notice appear electronically. Immigration financial
forms and bank evidence follow acceptance. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u4] [u18]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Math explicitly identifies Fall 2027 and December 1, 2026, with no Spring 2027 entry. Central handbook and
fellowship competitions are 2026-27; salary figures are 2025-26/2026-27, not 2027-28. Contract negotiation
update October 29, 2026 confirms future wage terms remain unsettled publicly. [u1] [u8] [u9] [u10] [u11]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [2027
confirmed]
December 1, 2026 for Fall 2027: application and all supporting materials, including letters. No public time/time
zone or separate grace period verified. Late or incomplete files generally will not be reviewed. No Spring 2027
entry. Ordinary support consideration accompanies the PhD application. [u1]
Test-score receipt [2027 confirmed]
Required English scores belong in the complete December 1, 2026 file unless exempt. Official reports must
come from the testing agency and be within two years of the proposed program start. ETS institution 1836;
IELTS and DET use the university's graduate admissions account. No separate later Math score deadline found;
contact the department for receipt confirmation. Neither GRE is required. [u1] [u2] [u3] [u8]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
A Math-specific Fall 2027 commitment deadline was not found. Follow the written offer and confirm any interim
check-ins. Other Illinois departments give inconsistent or legacy April dates; these do not establish
Mathematics' current deadline. New CGS 2027 participation must be verified separately rather than inferred
from old membership. [u27] [u28]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Central admission table: new TOEFL 4 limited / 5 full status; old TOEFL 79 / 103; IELTS 6.5 / 7.5; DET 115 / 135.
Math additionally lists old TOEFL 95 total and 22 speaking, or IELTS 6.5 speaking, without a new-scale
conversion. Math encourages scores even from exempt applicants. TA certification is separate: new TOEFL
speaking 5, old 24, or IELTS speaking 8; institutional oral assessment is an alternative. DET does not establish
TA qualification. Math permits temporary nonclassroom TA duties for old speaking 22-23, with full teaching
qualification within two years; new-scale equivalent unverified. TOEFL Home Edition/IELTS Online accepted
centrally; Essentials, MyBest and IELTS One Skill Retake are not. [u1] [u3] [u8] [u15]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Admission exemption likely applies through at least two years of postsecondary US study within five years of
entry, or a US degree received within five years. Thus an on-campus UChicago undergraduate normally
qualifies; confirm actual dates and study location. This inference is not individual approval. The exemption
does not waive the independent TA speaking requirement. Math's encouragement to submit scores remains
despite central exemption. [u1] [u3] [u8]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Not required for Fall 2027. The department does not explicitly say scores are prohibited, ignored, or
recommended; do not equate 'not required' with 'not considered.' The central portal supports score reporting,
but Math's treatment of voluntarily submitted scores is not publicly resolved. [u1] [u2]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
List every postsecondary institution where credit was earned and upload each transcript/academic record,
including the latest completed term. If awarded degree is not on transcript, include diploma/degree certificate.
Non-English records require originals and English translations; preserve grading keys. PDF or Word uploads
must be legible; scan guidance recommends grayscale under 200 dpi and use View Document to inspect.
Uploaded credentials are unofficial. Official versions are required during the first term after admission, though
the university may request them earlier. [u2] [u8]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
No separate mathematics-course list or applicant-written course descriptions are listed on the current PhD
checklist. The department explicitly says no program-specific questions or writing samples are required. Supply
full academic records; verify any live-portal optional course field rather than inventing a separate requirement.
[u1] [u2]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendation letters, preferably from mathematics professors who taught you or supervised your
research. Submit through the designated online recommendation system; Interfolio is not accepted. [u1] [u2]
[u4]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional reference is listed for ordinary TA consideration. Illinois Distinguished and Dean's Doctoral
Fellowships use departmental nominations, but the detail pages could not be fully read; additional nomination
references or questions remain unverified. Do not assume an extra applicant letter is required. [u1] [u6] [u11]
[u12] [u13]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Enter referees in the Recommendations section; letters can precede application submission. Public instructions
do not identify whether merely saving details immediately emails the invitation or a separate send action is
necessary. Check the live interface and ask referees before entering their details. [u2] [u4]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Applicant may submit before all references arrive; recommenders can upload afterward, but Math's December
1 deadline still applies. Invitations are not restricted to post-submission. Central FAQ supports adding or editing
recommender information and reminders. [u1] [u2] [u4]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Application status is available online, with reference management and reminder functions. A reference-specific
receipt badge or automatic applicant email for each letter is not described precisely in the public pages
reviewed; inspect the live checklist or contact the department if uncertain. [u4] [u18]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
A letter from another Illinois program or term may be reused only with the writer's explicit permission.
Importing the earlier recommendation does not send a new request, so do not import if a fresh letter is
intended. Referee email can be edited and reminders sent. An unsubmitted recommendation may be
excluded/reinstated; changing the access waiver requires excluding and re-adding the referee. Replacement of
an already submitted letter is not publicly established. [u2] [u4]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
Central instructions say most programs require a résumé/CV, but the Math PhD checklist does not clearly list it.
Prepare an academic CV and inspect the live required flag; no Math-specific public length or formatting limit
found. Do not import a separate internal-MS application's CV rules. [u1] [u2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required academic statement. Central guidance gives program-dependent maximums of 500-1,000 words; the
precise Math maximum is not publicly stated. Prompt paraphrase: preparation through
coursework/training/research; intellectual interests and questions; relevant faculty fit; how the program
supports academic/professional goals. Math calls its document a personal statement and asks for an honest,
brief, specific explanation of interest in Illinois. Treat that as the academic statement while also completing the
central personal short answers. Exact official wording is linked; no public font/spacing rule found. [u1] [u2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central personal short answers: each maximum 250 words. Questions 1 and 2 required, 3 and 4 optional.
Paraphrases: (1) pivotal experiences, opportunities or challenges, including access/financial barriers, shaping
